subject: Myth & Symbolism
subcategory: The World Tree and Cosmic Maps
title: Yggdrasil the World Ash
description: Learn Yggdrasil the World Ash in one minute.

hook.text: Yggdrasil is an enormous ash tree whose roots reach three wells and whose branches hold nine worlds.

buildup.text: An eagle sits at the top, a serpent gnaws the roots, and a squirrel runs between them carrying insults.

discovery.text: Odin hanged himself from Yggdrasil for nine nights to gain the runes. The tree is the source of all wisdom.

twist.text: Yggdrasil is slowly dying. The serpent's gnawing will eventually kill it. Even the cosmos has an expiration date.

climax.text: Yggdrasil is the most detailed world tree in mythology—alive, dying, and holding everything together at once.

punchline.text: Nine worlds. One tree. Everything hangs on it.

quiz.question: How many worlds does Yggdrasil hold in Norse mythology?
